# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute: I hold the manual (blue→green, green→yellow, red→red), I can hear speech, and my only outgoing channel is gestures, which only Deaf can see. The Blind cannot see colours at all, so the mapping in my head is useless unless Deaf gets it and relays it aloud to Blind. Deaf can speak, and I can hear — so we have a two-way loop, it just costs a round of latency.

Problem: gestures carry no inherent meaning yet. I need to bootstrap a code that Deaf can crack without me explaining it, then verify it over the next rounds using their spoken guesses and my 👍/👎.

My encoding plan: finger-counts as digits — ✊=0, ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3 (thumb+index+pinky). I index the four colours in rainbow order, zero-based: red=✊, yellow=☝, green=✌, blue=🤟. Then I send the three rules as "light 👉 wire" triples: 🤟👉✌ (blue→green), ✌👉☝ (green→yellow), ✊👉✊ (red→red). Zero-indexing is deliberately forced: the ✊👉✊ pair only makes sense if the sequence starts at zero, and rainbow is the most natural visual ordering for a sighted partner. If Deaf misreads the ordering, they'll voice a hypothesis and I'll confirm or deny next round.

I open with 👋🫵🤙 ("hello — you — call/speak") to tell Deaf to describe the bomb aloud, use 🤌 as a repeated section delimiter, and close with 👍👎🤝 to establish confirm/deny/agreed for our verification loop. Nothing here can cause a cut, so this message is safe: all risk sits with Blind, who can't act until Deaf instructs them.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🤙", "🤌", "✊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤌", "🤟", "👉", "✌", "🤌", "✌", "👉", "☝", "🤌", "✊", "👉", "✊", "🤌", "👍", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, first touch report. Under my hands: a display module, a light module, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. I cannot read the display, cannot tell if the light is lit, and no wire colour ever reaches me. You are my only voice: I never see gestures, so anything Deaf sees must reach me as your spoken words. Please speak, exactly, what the manual says about DISPLAY, LIGHT and WIRES, and what you and Deaf observe that those rules need. If you can, agree a small gesture code with Deaf and then speak its meanings to me. I will not cut until you tell me which position.
Deaf says: Bomb report for both of you: the display reads zero. The light is red. There are three wires, left to right: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is green. Mute, you hold the manual but you cannot speak, and Blind cannot see your hands, so you two have no direct line — sign everything to me and I will speak it aloud to Blind. Blind, you are our only hands; every instruction will reach you through my voice. Before you touch anything, align with me: wire one is the leftmost wire as I face the bomb, so stand beside me and face it the same way I do, then your left is my left. Blind, to answer me: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, one raised finger means wire one, two fingers wire two, three fingers wire three. Mute, your signs all reached me, but we share no code yet so I could not read them — my next message gives you one. Remember: I can never hear you, signs are your only way to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, our code — I say the meaning, you watch the hand: thumbs up [👍] yes. Thumb down [👎] no. Index finger up [☝] wire one. Two fingers [✌] wire two. Love-you hand, thumb, index and pinky out [🤟] wire three. Closed fist [✊] cut. Raised palm [✋] stop or wait. Handshake [🤝] understood. Now check the manual for a display reading zero, a red light, and wires red, yellow, green — tell me if zero matters — then sign me the exact instruction in this code and I will say it word for word to Blind. Sign me the handshake if you agree.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

Deaf's code is sound and — importantly — it is the one *they* proposed, so there is zero ambiguity on their side; my job is simply to adopt it, confirm, and pass the verdict. Reading the situation through their report: the display shows zero, but my manual contains only the light→wire table, no display rule at all, so zero is irrelevant — that gets a 👎. The light is red, and my manual says a red light means cut the wire of the same colour, red. Deaf reports wire one is red, wire two yellow, wire three green. So the defusing instruction is: cut wire one — in their code, ✊ (cut) then ☝ (wire one).

I sign it all to Deaf in one clean sequence: 🤝 (I agree to the code, and acknowledge their handshake), 👎 (no — the display reading does not matter, there is no display rule in my manual), then ✊☝ (cut wire one). Deaf can relay that verbatim to Blind. I keep it minimal: extra symbols only invite misreading, and Blind has promised not to cut until instructed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👎", "✊", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Status: I heard Deaf's report — display zero, light red, wires left to right red, yellow, green. You heard it too. But in two rounds you have sent me nothing: I never see your gestures, your signs to Deaf are wasted on me. I only ever hear your voice, and the manual exists for me only as your voice. Deaf does not need your words — Deaf sees the bomb. I do. So in your next turn, please SPEAK to me, plainly and completely: first, every rule in the manual about the three wires — every condition, and which colour or position to cut; second, what the display's digit means, especially zero; third, what the light's colour means, especially red; fourth, any labels or markings the manual says to read, and what they show. Spell out every colour, quote every condition, do not summarise. Also tell Deaf in signs, once you share a code: Blind cannot see you, so I cannot stand beside you to copy your left and right. My hands feel three wire slots numbered 1, 2, 3 and no geometry beyond that, so we adopt this assumption: my 1, 2, 3 are your leftmost, middle, rightmost. If any manual rule depends on position rather than colour, say so aloud — then we stop and fix orientation before I cut. I will not cut anything until your voice gives me the rules.
Deaf says: Blind, this is your instruction for now: HOLD. Do not touch or cut anything yet. Mute has replied and I am locking down the exact instruction before you act — one more exchange. The bomb is unchanged: display zero, red light, wires red, yellow, green left to right. While you wait, it would help us if you speak aloud what the wires feel like under your fingers — how many there are, thick or thin, what they attach to — because Mute can hear you and can match your description against the manual. Also confirm: facing the bomb the same way I do, the first wire on your left should be the one I call wire one.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs as: understood — no — cut wire one. Answer me with exactly two signs, in this order. First sign: thumbs up [👍] if the display reading zero has NO special rule, or thumbs down [👎] if the manual gives zero a rule I must know. Second sign: thumbs up [👍] if the instruction is exactly this — cut the leftmost wire, the red one, wire one as I face the bomb — or thumbs down [👎] if that is wrong, and if it is wrong, follow your thumbs down immediately with the corrected signs. To be full in your picture: the bomb shows only the display, the light, and the three wires; nothing else is printed on it.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

Deaf asked for exactly two signs, and both answers are unambiguous from my manual. Sign one: my manual contains no display rule of any kind — the only table in it maps light colour to wire colour — so a display reading of zero carries no rule: 👍. Sign two: the light is red, red light means cut the red wire, and Deaf sees wire one (leftmost) as the red one, so "cut the leftmost wire, the red one, wire one" is exactly correct: 👍.

Blind's plea for me to speak cannot be granted — I am the Mute, I have no voice at all; gestures to Deaf are my entire output, and Deaf must remain my mouth. Deaf already knows this and has promised to relay verbatim, so the loop Deaf → Blind is the right conduit, and I will not muddy the two-sign protocol they explicitly requested. I also note for my own check: my manual's rules key on colour only, never position, so Blind's worry about left/right orientation does not affect the rule itself — it only matters that Deaf's "wire one is red" maps onto Blind's slot 1, which is exactly the verification Deaf is running with Blind's tactile description. The cut instruction itself is safe to release.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
```

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Holding as ordered, nothing touched. Tactile report for you to match against the manual: under my fingers there are exactly three wires, entering three parallel slots in one row on the bomb's face, numbered by me 1, 2, 3 in a fixed order. To my touch the three wires feel alike — similar thickness, similar insulation, no knots, tags or texture differences I can find. Each wire runs from its slot inward toward the bomb's body; I cannot trace where they terminate. Answer my questions with single signs, in this exact order. Question one: you understood this whole message — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question two: your thumbs down last round meant the left-right alignment is wrong — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question three: you can stand facing the front of the bomb as I do, so that your left hand is on the same side as the end where the red wire sits — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question four: you can feel three separate wires — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question five: the wires feel different from each other by touch, thick or thin, smooth or rough — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Question six: you are able and willing to speak aloud, so Mute can hear your descriptions, even though I never can — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. For orientation: the display and the red light sit on the upper part of the front face, the light beside the display, and the three wires run in a horizontal row beneath them. If none of my questions match what your thumbs down meant, answer thumbs down to all and I will ask differently next round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your answer was received and clear: no rule for display zero, and cut wire one, the leftmost red. But Blind signed thumbs down to my alignment check, so the cut is on hold until we fix left and right — I have just sent Blind six questions. Meanwhile answer me with signs in this exact order. One: sign the wire NUMBER the manual says to cut — [☝] for the red, [✌] for the yellow, [🤟] for the green. Two: [👍] if the rule depends on the wires alone, [👎] if the display reading or the light color changes which wire is safe. Three: [👍] if cutting that wire is safe right now with the bomb exactly as it reads — display zero, light red, wires red, yellow, green — or [👎] if something must be checked or done first, and if so, explain using these new signs: [👌] means the light, [🤏] means the display, [✋] means wait, [✊] means cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝]

The bomb per the manual: the red light is the only key that matters — red light → cut the red wire, which in Deaf's view is wire one; the display's zero has no rule anywhere in my book. Deaf's three questions deserve exact-order, literal answers. One: the wire the manual says to cut is the red one, which Deaf anchored to ☝ — so ☝. Two: 👎, truthfully, because my manual's rule is keyed to the light's colour, not to the wires alone — if the light were green I'd order the yellow wire, if blue, the green. Deaf can infer it's the light specifically, since they already have my word there's no display rule. Three: 👍 — with the bomb exactly as reported (zero, red light, red/yellow/green), the manual demands nothing further before cutting the red wire; no hidden precondition exists to hunt for. The only thing standing between us and the cut is the physical left/right mapping, which is not a manual matter and which Deaf is already settling with Blind's landmark check — and Deaf has rightly kept the cut on hold until then.

Blind's repeated request for my voice I cannot satisfy — I have none, by nature; my only output is gestures Deaf can see, and Deaf remains my mouth. Blind's landmark question ("which module sits nearest wire one?") is one only Deaf, the sighted one, can answer, and Deaf has already begun describing the layout to Blind. I add nothing beyond the three requested signs: Deaf asked for exact order, and stray symbols could corrupt the parse of a safety-critical exchange.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎", "👍"])
```

Deaf's five questions all have crisp manual answers, in order: (1) 👎 — the display digit appears nowhere in my book; (2) 👍 — the rule keys on the light's colour alone; (3) 👎 — since no display rule exists, the correct wire cannot change with the display; (4) 👎 — my manual has nothing about wires distinguishable or grip-able by touch, its only content is the three-row colour table; (5) 👎 — no precondition like opening a panel exists. Deaf's new signs 🫲 (left) and 🫱 (right) plus 👌 (light) and 🤏 (display) let me encode that question perfectly. Then you signed: light, display, left, right. Answer in this exact order. Since Blind's 1-2-3 = Deaf's left-middle-right and Blind can find both modules by touch, Deaf answering that one fact aloud lets Blind prove the mapping without trust.
